channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.description: Iran reports ships are being hit by mines it had laid in the Strait of Hormuz; says talks with Oman over control of the Strait are at an advanced stage; Houthis claim to have downed a Saudi drone Iran halts ‘retaliatory strikes’ after lull in U. item.title: Russian and Ukrainian strikes kill at least 10
item.description: The strikes come a day after 20 people were killed on both sides of the frontline, with both Kyiv and Moscow intensifying attacks while diplomacy to end the war. launched by Russia in 2022. is at a deadlock. Russian and Ukrainian strikes kill at least 10.

item.title: Honduras ex-President Hernandez to return home after Trump pardon
item.description: He is expected to appear ‌before a court on August 3 to face charges of fraud ‌and ⁠money laundering. An arrest warrant issued against him was suspended in ⁠June, meaning he will not be detained upon arrival Honduras ex-President Hernandez to return home after Trump pardon.

item.title: Germany says fatal Berlin Pride attack believed to be an act of Islamic extremist terror
item.description: The suspect in Saturday night’s (July 25) attack remains at large. Authorities issued a wanted notice and warned people against approaching Abdul Ballout, a German citizen with Lebanese roots, saying that he may be armed and dangerous. Germany says fatal Berlin Pride attack believed to be an act of Islamic extremist terror.

item.title: 10 killed after Typhoon Noul makes landfall in southern China
item.description: Noul, the 12th and the strongest typhoon to hit China so far this year, made landfall at Huizhou city in Guangdong around 3:50 a. m., bringing gale-force winds and heavy rain to large parts of the region 10 killed after Typhoon Noul makes landfall in southern China.

item.title: Venezuelan men sue aviation firms who flew them to notorious Salvadorian jail
item.description: Exclusive: CSI Aviation and GlobalX accused of violating civil rights as part of Trump immigration crackdownVenezuelan men sent last year to a notorious Salvadorian terrorism prison by the Trump administration are suing the US aviation companies that transported them there. Venezuela men sue aviation firms who flew them to notorious Salvadorian jail. Venezuelan men sue aviation firms who flew them to notorious Salvadorian jail.

item.title: Street-smart youth take their declaration to the UN
item.description: When Samantha Richards and Angela Hifume walked into the Hall of Flags at United Nations Headquarters last week, they carried more than a folder of paper. They carried the voices of hundreds of street-connected children who had never expected anyone to listen. Street-smart youth take their declaration to the UN.

item.title: UN chief hails Syria’s ‘moment of possibility’ on first visit since fall of Assad regime
item.description: Syria has an opportunity not only to recover from conflict but to build “a future that is more stable, more inclusive and more prosperous for all Syrians”, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said in Damascus on Saturday as he began a landmark visit to the country. UN chief hails Syria’s ‘moment of possibility’ on first visit since fall of Assad regime.

item.title: Attacks On Chinese Projects Test China-Pakistan 'Iron Brotherhood' In Balochistan
item.description: China's investments in Pakistan's Balochistan are increasingly at risk as attacks by separatists are on the rise in the impoverished region. The worsening security situation has strained ties between the Iron Brothers, raising concerns over the future of Beijing's investments in Pakistan. Attacks On Chinese Projects Test China-Pakistan 'Iron Brotherhood' In Balochistan.

item.title: Politicians vs generals: Ukraine’s long, hidden war within
item.description: The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelensky, has dismissed the country’s commander-in-chief, Oleksandr Syrskyi, after a turbulent week in which he also removed his defense minister, Mykhailo Fedorov. The dismissal of the popular defense minister, who is credited by many as the brains behind Ukraine’s successful drone strategy, brought thousands onto the streets in protest. item.title: Trump Says Iran 'Far More Serious' In Talks, Even As Attacks Intensify, Widen In Region
item.description: US President Donald ⁠Trump ⁠said Washington and Tehran were still conducting negotiations to end their conflict -- even as attacks intensified throughout the region, further threatening to widen the conflict into a full-blown Middle East war. Trump Says Iran 'Far More Serious' In Talks, Even As Attacks Intensify, Widen In Region.

item.title: Iranian Sisters, 20, Tried In High-Profile Case Tied To January Protests
item.description: Sixteen people are facing charges connected to protests in Isfahan in January, during which a colonel in Iran's Revolutionary Guard was killed. Rights defenders are raising concerns about the legitimacy of the case, including the charges against 20-year-old sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi. Iranian Sisters, Aged 20, Tried In High-Profile Case Tied To January Protests. Iranian Sisters, 20, Tried In High-Profile Case Tied To January Protests.

item.title: Russia's 'Axis Of Upheaval' Is Built To Last Beyond Ukraine, Analyst Kendall-Taylor Says
item.description: Russia's deepening partnerships with China, Iran, and North Korea represent one of the most significant geopolitical realignments driven by the war in Ukraine. Yet according to Andrea Kendall-Taylor, viewing this grouping through the lens of a traditional military alliance misses the bigger picture. Russia's 'Axis Of Upheaval' Is Built To Last Beyond Ukraine, Analyst Kendall-Taylor Says.

item.title: Guyanese authorities confirm death of 72 people in sinking of coastal ferry
item.description: Guyanese authorities confirm 72 deaths after a state ferry capsized off the coast, leaving 179 people aboard. Of the estimated 179 people aboard, 76 were rescued as efforts continue to salvage the ship and recover all bodiesThe confirmed death toll from the recent capsizing of a state ferry off Guyana’s coast has risen to 72, with more bodies recovered as a multinational team struggle to salvage the partially submerged vessel. Of the estimated 179 people aboard, 76 people were rescued.

item.description: Earlier this month, the Supreme Leader of Iran, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, was buried in his hometown of Mashhad after a four-day ceremony. Many international delegations were present, but each country will have chosen their representatives with the utmost care. item.title: ‘Women do not stop giving birth in an emergency’ – one month after Venezuela quakes
item.description: One month after twin earthquakes rocked Venezuela, thousands of women and girls continue to face difficulty in accessing essential healthcare and protection services, a senior official with the UN reproductive and sexual health agency UNFPA said on Friday. ‘Women do not stop giving birth in an emergency’ – one month after Venezuela quakes.

item.title: After an Ebola centre was attacked, peacekeepers moved in next door
item.description: A new mobile UN peacekeeping base in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has allowed local authorities to continue responding to the fast-moving Ebola outbreak there after violence disrupted the work of medics at a treatment centre set up to contain the spread. After an Ebola centre was attacked, peacekeepers moved in next door.

item.title: In El Obeid, Sudanese women face drones by day, rape by night, to reach water
item.description: In El Obeid, women and girls now face an impossible choice over something as basic as a bucket of water: risk a drone strike by collecting it in daylight, or risk rape by waiting until dark. In El Obeid, Sudanese women face drones by day, rape by night, to reach water.
